title: Television: John Lennon and Yoko Ono on The Mike Douglas Show | 1972
content:
John Lennon and Yoko Ono filmed the third of five appearances on The Mike Douglas Show on 20 January 1972.

The shows were filmed at the KYW-TV studio at 1619 Walnut Street in Philadelphia. The couple’s other appearances were filmed on 14, 18, and 27 January, and 4 February 1972, and broadcast over a week from 14 February.

This episode was broadcast on 17 February. It began with Lennon performing ‘Imagine’ with Elephant’s Memory backing him.

In the first episode, Ono introduced ‘Mend Piece’, telling the audience that a broken tea cup would be gradually mended over the course of the episodes until it was fully fixed. It was brought back during this show, in an almost completed form.

Lennon spoke to Douglas about his upbringing in Liverpool, his absent father and late mother, explaining how she taught him to play the banjo to give him a start as a musician.

The other guests were a decidedly mixed bag. The first were comedy ensemble Ace Trucking Co, who were followed by Marsha Martin, organiser of the National Black Youth Conference. Broadway performer Vivian Reed sang ‘Everybody’s Talkin” and ‘His Eye Is On The Sparrow’, and Donald Williams from Stanford Medical School discussed sickle cell anaemia.

Lennon and Ono were keen to keep a radical politics thread running through their appearances. Guesting on this show was Bobby Seale, who co-founded the Black Panther Party with Huey P Newton.

At the end of the show, the ‘Mrs Lennon’ sequence from the forthcoming Imagine film was shown.
